verdict: The easiest of the four to start: a public integration gets OAuth credentials once you fill in a few details. Notion's own docs say the authorization URL appears only after the public connection is submitted for review, and they don't say how long that review takes.
start_now: Low risk to wait. Have a privacy policy, terms page and support email ready before you start.

cases.case: Review before other workspaces can connect
cases.outcome: Notion's docs mention submitting for review; duration and criteria not published

steps.title: Create a new integration and choose Public
Fill website, privacy policy, terms and support email
steps.detail: Needed before the client ID and secret appear.

steps.title: Choose capabilities
steps.detail: Notion uses capability toggles (read, update, insert content) instead of OAuth scopes.

steps.title: Add your redirect URL and copy credentials
steps.detail: Users pick which pages to share during consent.

blockers.text: The authorization URL only appears after the public connection is submitted for review (Notion docs). How long that takes isn't stated.
Installation scope (any workspace or selected ones) is set when you create the connection and can't be changed later.
Users choose pages at consent time. Your agent sees nothing the user didn't share.

agent_can: Pick the minimum capabilities for your features
Check your policy and terms URLs exist
you_must: Host a privacy policy and terms page
unverified: How long Notion's review of a public connection takes, and what it checks
Whether a hands-on report of instant credentials (2023) still matches today's flow
